mesoscaleDiscussions.areas: Eastern Nebraska into southwest Iowa and northern Missouri
mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Elevated thunderstorms may pose a risk of isolated large hail and severe gusts through the overnight hours for parts of far eastern Nebraska into southwest Iowa and northern/northwest Missouri. The severe risk is expected to generally remain sufficiently isolated to preclude the need for a watch.

details.label: Areas affected
details.text: Eastern Nebraska into southwest Iowa and northern Missouri

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Convection has been percolating across southwest IA over the past hour, and is largely being driven by modest isentropic ascent between 925-850 mb on the eastern fringe of a low-level thermal ridge where capping is weaker. Although this activity is displaced to the east of greater instability over NE/KS, latest mesoanalysis estimates and the 00 UTC OAX RAOB show MUCAPE values of 2000-3000 J/kg from eastern NE into northern MO. Additionally, mid-level winds on the order of 50 knots are supporting effective bulk shear values of similar magnitude oriented along the buoyancy gradient. This thermodynamic and kinematic environment is conducive for organized severe convection, and recent radar trends appear to reflect this - a few deeper cores within the cluster have exhibited vertical ice signatures consistent with severe hail. The expectation over the next several hours is for additional thunderstorm development across southwest IA into adjacent portions of north/northwest MO with additional re-development probable across far eastern NE based on latest GOES IR trends. Storm motions along the zone of initiation will promote destructive storm interactions that will likely limit the overall propensity for long-lived/intense convection. However, given the ambient environment a few strong/severe thunderstorms appear likely through the early morning hours - mainly posing a threat for large hail and perhaps severe gusts. Recent RRFS solutions appear to be capturing this overall signal well (even if a little delayed) and suggest the overall severe threat should be isolated in nature, but could persist to around 12 UTC.

mesoscaleDiscussions.areas: Southern North Dakota into northeast South Dakota and far western Minnesota
mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Elevated thunderstorms developing along the North Dakota/South Dakota border may continue to intensify and grow upscale over the coming hours. If upscale growth can occur, a more pronounced severe risk may emerge and require watch issuance. Convective trends are being monitored.

details.label: Areas affected
details.text: Southern North Dakota into northeast South Dakota and far western Minnesota

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Deep convection has begun to emerge along the ND/SD border over the past 30-45 minutes with additional towering, but weaker, convection noted in GOES IR imagery over southern and eastern ND. Similar to previous attempts at sustained deep convection, this activity appears to largely be driven by increasing isentropic ascent within the warm advection branch of a weak cyclone over the western Dakotas - augmented by a slight uptick in the nocturnal jet strength over the past hour (per regional VWPs). This emerging convection resides on the northern periphery of a buoyancy reservoir with MUCAPE values as high as 4000 J/kg analyzed downstream into SD. Additionally, 50-60 knot effective bulk shear was recently sampled by the 00 UTC BIS and ABR RAOBs, suggesting that intensification/organization of this convection is likely. Given the trends in IR imagery, adequate forcing for ascent, and downstream environment, it appears possible that some severe threat will emerge over the next few hours along the ND/SD border. Latest runs of the RRFS appear to be capturing convective trends well and suggest additional convection will manifest over the next 1-2 hours before growing upscale. If/when this occurs, the potential for severe hail and severe wind gusts will likely increase. Convective trends are being monitored, and watch issuance may be required if convective coverage increases.

statements.headline: Severe Weather Statement
statements.summary: Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees. Locations impacted include... California, Brownsville, Fredericktown-Millsboro, Jefferson Boro, Isabella, West Brownsville, Deemston, Republic, Marianna, Rices Landing, New Salem, Grindstone, Clarksville and Centerville.
